text: AfriDish serves as a marketplace where African food businesses can showcase and sell their products to millions of food lovers in Canada.
Stanley Ezenwafor is the founder of AfriDish.
Stanley Ezenwafor has a degree in Computer Networks and Telecommunications.
Stanley Ezenwafor has seven years of experience in project management and software development.
The funding goal for AfriDish was $10,592.
The project's funding was unsuccessful as the goal was not reached by April 12, 2024.
The funding period for AfriDish was from February 12, 2024, to April 12, 2024.
Stanley Ezenwafor observed a significant gap in the support for African food businesses in Canada.
AfriDish aims to provide high visibility, value, and profitability for African and Caribbean food businesses.
AfriDish is a technology platform designed to empower African and Caribbean food businesses in Canada.
AfriDish serves as a marketplace where African food businesses can showcase and sell their products to millions of food lovers across Canada.
AfriDish aims to provide high visibility, value, and profitability for African food businesses.
AfriDish functions as the UberEats and Instacart for Black food businesses in Canada.
The web e-commerce platform of AfriDish is ready to launch by April.
AfriDish requires additional funding to accelerate its marketing strategies and reach more businesses and customers nationwide.
AfriDish is committed to innovation, cultural celebration, and economic empowerment.
AfriDish faces cybersecurity threats as an operational risk.
AfriDish plans to implement robust cybersecurity measures, regular audits, user education, and collaboration with experts as mitigation for cybersecurity threats.
AfriDish faces risks related to changes in regulations or non-compliance.
To mitigate regulatory compliance risks, AfriDish will stay informed, work closely with legal advisors, and ensure alignment with regulations.
AfriDish faces logistical challenges such as delays or transportation issues.
AfriDish plans to build strong relationships with logistics partners, resolve issues promptly, and implement tracking systems to mitigate logistical challenges.
AfriDish faces user challenges in onboarding as a risk.
To mitigate user onboarding challenges, AfriDish will provide comprehensive onboarding resources, tutorials, responsive customer support, and continuous improvement based on user feedback.
The project seeks funding for AI technology.
The project will obtain consent from individuals whose works or information are incorporated into the database or source.
Kickstarter encourages sustainable practices through its Environmental Resources Center.
AfriDish will implement continuous innovation to adapt to changing market dynamics and user preferences.
AfriDish was built with scalability in mind to handle increased traffic and transaction volumes.
AfriDish will prioritize customer feedback and satisfaction to tailor the platform to user needs.
User challenges in onboarding are identified as a risk.
Comprehensive onboarding resources, tutorials, and responsive customer support will be implemented as mitigation for onboarding challenges.
Continuous improvement based on user feedback will be part of the onboarding strategy.
The platform will prioritize customer feedback and satisfaction to tailor its services to the needs of businesses and consumers.
AfriDish will collaborate with key stakeholders, such as African food businesses, delivery services, and industry influencers.
These partnerships will help extend the reach and enhance the value proposition of AfriDish.
AfriDish will explore opportunities for diversification, including expanding into related verticals or offering additional services.
By diversifying revenue streams and market segments, AfriDish aims to mitigate risks and maintain steady growth over the long term.
The scalability of the platform ensures that it remains robust and efficient as it expands to serve more businesses and customers.
